coffee-ethiopia-yirgacheffe.name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe
coffee-ethiopia-yirgacheffe.description: Floral, citrusy high-altitude Arabica with bright acidity and tea-like body. Light–medium roast.
coffee-ethiopia-yirgacheffe.history: From the birthplace of coffee in Ethiopia's highlands, Yirgacheffe is known as the 'champagne of coffees' with centuries-old heirloom varieties.
benefits: Rich in antioxidants and chlorogenic acids

coffee-kenya-aa.name: Kenya AA
coffee-kenya-aa.description: Bright acidity with distinctive blackcurrant and berry notes. Washed process for clean cup profile.
coffee-kenya-aa.history: Kenyan coffee cultivation dates back to the 19th century, with AA grade representing the largest bean size and highest quality in the East African grading system.
benefits: May reduce risk of chronic diseases
ingredients: 100% Arabica coffee beans (Coffea arabica, SL28 & SL34 varieties)

coffee-tanzania-peaberry.name: Tanzania Peaberry
coffee-tanzania-peaberry.description: Rounded sweetness with cocoa finish and vibrant acidity. Unique peaberry mutation creates concentrated flavor.
coffee-tanzania-peaberry.history: From the slopes of Mount Kilimanjaro and Meru, Tanzanian coffee has been cultivated since the 16th century. Peaberry beans occur naturally when only one seed develops in the coffee cherry.
benefits: Rich in essential nutrients and antioxidants

coffee-nigeria-robusta.name: Nigeria Robusta
coffee-nigeria-robusta.description: Bold, full-bodied coffee with earthy notes and higher caffeine content. Perfect for strong brews and espresso.
coffee-nigeria-robusta.history: Coffee cultivation in Nigeria dates back to the 19th century, with robusta varieties thriving in the country's tropical climate and contributing to West Africa's coffee heritage.
benefits: Higher caffeine content for sustained energy
Rich in antioxidants and chlorogenic acid
